label: Adenoid_Cystic_Carcinoma
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma (ACC) frequently occurs in major and minor salivary glands.
- Histologically characterized by cribriform, tubular, and solid growth patterns.
- Noted for perineural invasion and potential for late distant metastasis.
- Typically involves MYB-NFIB fusion.
- Prognosis varies; recurrences and distant metastases may occur years after treatment.

## Terminology
- Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma (ACC).
- Not recommended: Cylindroma, Basaloid carcinoma.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Cribriform, tubular, and solid patterns.
  - Evidence of perineural invasion.
- **Desirable:**
  - MYB-NFIB fusion presence.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- MYB (6q23) gene rearrangements are characteristic.
  - MYB-NFIB fusion present in a significant number of cases.

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:**
  - Primarily affects adults; middle-aged women slightly more affected.
- **Site:**
  - Major salivary glands (especially parotid) and minor salivary glands.
- **Presentation:**
  - Painless, slow-growing mass; facial nerve involvement may indicate poor prognosis.
- **Prognosis:**
  - High recurrence rate; distant metastasis common, affecting survival.

## Macroscopic
- Well-circumscribed mass but infiltrative growth patterns at the microscopic level.
- Size can vary, often firm upon palpation.

## Microscopic
- Cribriform pattern is classic, resembling Swiss-cheese.
- Tubular and solid variants exist; solid type has a worse prognosis.
- Perineural invasion is a significant feature.
- Cells are typically basaloid.

  ![Cribriform pattern](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/salivaryglandsadenoidcysticXu03new.jpg)

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemistry (IHC):**
  - Positive for cytokeratins (CAM5.2, AE1/AE3).
  - Myoepithelial markers include p63, SMA, and S100.
- **Molecular:**
  - MYB-NFIB fusion frequently detected using molecular techniques.

## Differential Diagnosis
- **Basal Cell Adenocarcinoma:**
  - Lack of perineural invasion and MYB rearrangement.
- **Pleomorphic Adenoma:**
  - Presence of chondromyxoid stroma.
- **Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma:**
  - Mucin-producing cells and cystic areas.
- **Polymorphous Adenocarcinoma:**
  - More uniform nuclei, lacks cribriform pattern.
- **Sialoblastoma:**
  - Primitive histological features; occurs in younger patients ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Sialoblastoma.html)).
- **Epithelial-Myoepithelial Carcinoma:**
  - Biphasic and/or clear cell morphology ([WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Epithelial_Myoepithelial_Carcinoma.html)).

For more detailed information, see [WHO](https://storage.googleapis.com/pathology-hub-0/WHO/WHO_HTML/HN/Sialoblastoma.html) and [Pathoutlines](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/topic/salivaryglandsadenoidcystic.html).

cards.title: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma definition: HPV-related multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma (HMSC) is an epithelial neoplasm exhibiting features of both surface-derived and minor salivary gland–derived elements, harbouring transcriptionally active HPV. related_terminology: Acceptable: HPV-associated multiphenotypic sinonasal carcinoma. Not recommended: HPV-related carcinoma with adenoid cystic–like features. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a carcinoma composed of basaloid type cells; high-risk HPV by HPV-specific assay (not p16 alone); myoepithelial differentiation by immunohistochemistry. Desirable: sinonasal tract location; ductal differentiation; overlying squamous dysplasia.

cards.title: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma Section: cytology FNAB smears can show poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma or salivary duct carcinoma, or other salivary gland carcinomas including mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma, or the FNAB may show PA, depending on sampling. It is uncommon that both components are identified, and necrosis in an otherwise pleomorphic adenoma may be the only clue apart from a previous history of a longstanding mass or previous biopsy.

cards.title: Sialoblastoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Sialoblastoma definition: Sialoblastoma is a low-grade malignant primitive salivary gland anlage neoplasm. related_terminology: Not recommended: embryoma; basaloid adenocarcinoma; congenital basal cell adenoma; congenital hybrid basal cell adenoma; adenoid cystic carcinoma. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a salivary gland malignancy showing primitive solid organoid nests; basaloid epithelial cells with vesicular chromatin; cuboidal to columnar ductal cells. Desirable: dividing fibrous stroma and peripheral palisading.

cards.title: Sialoblastoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Sialoblastoma Section: differential_diagnosis The primitive histological features and the patients young age help to differentiate sialoblastoma from other basaloid salivary gland tumours such as basal cell adenoma/adenocarcinoma, adenoid cystic carcinoma, and adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma.

cards.title: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma Section: differential_diagnosis The differential diagnosis includes other salivary gland tumours with biphasic and/or clear cell morphology, such as adenoid cystic carcinoma, basal cell adenocarcinoma, pleomorphic adenoma, myoepithelial carcinoma, and clear cell carcinoma.

cards.title: Cystadenoma — Mucinous cystadenoma is rare; lacks architectural and nuclear atypia
cards.excerpt:
Consider unicystic mucoepidermoid carcinoma in the differential diagnosis
Prominent multiloculated / multicystic growth pattern gives a low power appearance of more lumens than epithelial cells
Simple papillary projections and true papillae are common; however, complex papillary tufting should alert the pathologist to other differential diagnoses (e.g. intraductal carcinoma)
Immunohistochemical stains are useful to rule out macrocystic secretory carcinoma and intercalated type intraductal carcinoma (Head Neck Pathol 2015;9:354, Oral and Maxillofacial Pathology Journal 2017;8:28, Surg Pathol Clin 2021;14:53)
Microscopic (histologic) imagesContributed by Aditya Talwar, M.D.

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:
Characterized by a propensity of perineural invasion, high frequency of local and distant recurrence and poor long term prognosis (Eur J Cancer 2015;51:2768, Head Neck 2017;39:456, Braz J Otorhinolaryngol 2015;81:329, Head Neck 2014;36:998)
5 year overall survival 55 - 89%
15 year or 20 year survival is dismal, in the range of 20 - 40%
Rates of local recurrence and distant metastasis are 16 - 67% and 8 - 46%
Lung is most common site of distant metastasis (Head Neck 2017;39:456)

cards.title: Adenoid cystic carcinoma — Lung metastases
cards.excerpt:
Prognostic factors
Independent prognostic predictors include AJCC TNM staging, margin status, high mitotic index (defined as ≥ 5 per 10 high power fields) and solid architecture (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422)
Presence and percentage of solid architecture reflects clinical outcome and should be reported in the pathology report
Some studies showed that the presence but not the percentage of solid growth is an independent predictor for adverse outcome (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:1422, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Ora Radio 2013;115:368, Head Neck 2017;39:456)
Other studies show that tumors with higher percentage of solid pattern, defined as 30% or more, are associated with increased risk of recurrence and decreased survival (Cancer 1984;54:1062, Cancer 1978;42:265)

cards.excerpt:
Complete surgical resection with appropriate margins is the mainstream treatment
Most patients receive adjuvant radiation therapy given the high rate of local recurrence and dismal long term survival

cards.title: Salivary duct cyst — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Complete excision along with the feeding minor salivary gland is curative (Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 1987;113:51)
Iatrogenic intraoperative damage to neighboring salivary gland parenchyma may contribute to the development of postoperative mucocele (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Partial or total removal of feeding major salivary glands may be required (Pediatr Dermatol 2008;25:308)
Chlorhexidine mouth rinse or oral antibiotics for secondarily infected salivary duct cysts (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)
Sialagogues may decrease the risk of salivary stasis within dilated ducts by stimulating salivary flow

Mucoid secretion surrounded by a bilayer of cuboidal or columnar stratified salivary duct epithelium (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)

cards.title: Sclerosing polycystic adenoma — Pathophysiology
cards.excerpt:
Originally believed to be a reactive, nonneoplastic process resembling fibrocystic changes of the breast but evidence suggests it is likely neoplastic (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)
Recurrence rate of up to 30% (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Demonstration of clonality in 6 cases using the human androgen receptor assay (HUMARA) (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Targeted next generation sequencing demonstrated mutations in genes that are well established to be drivers in human neoplasms (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)

cards.title: Sclerosing polycystic adenoma — Microscopic (histologic) description
cards.excerpt:
Circumscribed with preservation of lobular architecture (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Composed of irregularly distributed bilayered ducts and acini within a sclerotic stroma (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)
Ducts range from small tubules to ectatic spaces; may contain secretory material or foamy macrophages (Head Neck Pathol 2020;14:630)
Ductal cells can have vacuolated, foamy, apocrine and mucous appearances (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)
Hyperplastic ductal epithelium forming solid, microcystic and cribriform structures (Am J Surg Pathol 2017;41:e33)
Small eosinophilic globules of basement membrane-like material in some cribriform areas (i.e. collagenous spherulosis) (Am J Surg Pathol 1996;20:161)
Acini contain numerous, coarse eosinophilic, periodic acid-Schiff positive, intracytoplasmic granules (Am J Surg Pathol 2006;30:939)

cards.title: Salivary duct cyst — Clinical features
cards.excerpt:
Dome shaped, sessile, slow growing but asymptomatic nodule (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)
1 - 3 cm but have been reported to grow up to 10 cm (J Oral Sci 2001;43:9)
Fluctuant to palpation but usually painless, some may feel firmer especially if a sialolith is present (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Mucus or pus may be expressed from dilated ductal orifices when palpated if secondarily infected (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)

cards.title: Salivary duct cyst — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Complete excision along with the feeding minor salivary gland is curative (Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 1987;113:51)
Iatrogenic intraoperative damage to neighboring salivary gland parenchyma may contribute to the development of postoperative mucocele (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Partial or total removal of feeding major salivary glands may be required (Pediatr Dermatol 2008;25:308)
Chlorhexidine mouth rinse or oral antibiotics for secondarily infected salivary duct cysts (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)
Sialagogues may decrease the risk of salivary stasis within dilated ducts by stimulating salivary flow

cards.title: Salivary duct cyst — Gross imagesImages hosted on other servers
cards.excerpt:
Smooth firm labial noduleMicroscopic (histologic) description
Mucoid secretion surrounded by a bilayer of cuboidal or columnar stratified salivary duct epithelium (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Cyst lining may have papillary folds into the lumen (Head Neck Pathol 2017;11:469)
May have squamous or oncocytic metaplasia of cyst lining, especially with more severe obstruction (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Sialolith and bacteria causing secondary infection may be present among the submitted tissue (Head Neck Pathol 2017;11:469)
Feeding salivary gland, if included, has obstructive changes with variable ductal dilation, lymphocytic infiltrate with periductal pattern and fibrosis (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)

Mucoid secretion surrounded by a bilayer of cuboidal or columnar stratified salivary duct epithelium (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Cyst lining may have papillary folds into the lumen (Head Neck Pathol 2017;11:469)
May have squamous or oncocytic metaplasia of cyst lining, especially with more severe obstruction (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1964;18:191)
Sialolith and bacteria causing secondary infection may be present among the submitted tissue (Head Neck Pathol 2017;11:469)
Feeding salivary gland, if included, has obstructive changes with variable ductal dilation, lymphocytic infiltrate with periductal pattern and fibrosis (Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1984;58:692)

Mucocele/mucus extravasation phenomenon/ranula/plunging rannula/mucus escape reaction
There is no true salivary gland duct epithelial lining and instead this is mimicked by epithelioid macrophages (muciphages) at the periphery of the extravasated mucin
